column4: The preceding surah supplies the transitive counterpart to 92:2: daylight جَلَّاهَا makes the sun manifest, whereas in 92:2 the day itself تَجَلَّىٰ.
The exact covering verb has its object here: night يَغْشَىٰهَا covers the sun, clarifying the deliberately objectless يَغْشَىٰ of 92:1.
This single ayah joins rivers placed through the earth with يُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ; it uniquely gathers the section's river-cut earth and night-covering-day images.
God يـُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ in a creation scene that closes by assigning both creation and command to Him, directly joining 92:1 with the creating of 92:3.
Daylight is peeled from night like a skin, نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ, reversing the angle of the night laid over what is visible in 92:1.
The only other divine تَجَلَّىٰ stages disclosure to the mountain; its crushing force shows the protective limit implicit in a covering.
وَجْهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ means the beginning or first face of the day, exactly realizing the dictionary image placed beside وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ in the section.
Night and day are two signs: the night-sign is effaced and the day-sign is made مُبْصِرَةً, directly coupling daylight with visibility and discernment.
God is فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ, the splitter of dawn, and makes night repose; this stages both the section's cracked opening and its claim that the cover can be merciful.
The exact noun غِشَاوَةٌ lies over rejecting eyes, turning the night-covering root into the perceptual membrane developed in the section.
A غِشَاوَةً is placed over the desire-worshipper's sight and is followed immediately by the question of who can guide him, joining veil and guidance exactly as the prose does.
Barriers stand before and behind the rejecters and فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ leaves them unable to see, a spatial enactment of remaining beneath the covering.
Moses sees a fire and hopes أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى; fire, sight, and guidance meet in one scene as they do through 92:12 and 92:14 in the section.
After grief, reassuring drowsiness يَغْشَىٰ a group of believers; the same covering action protects rather than blinds or punishes.
God causes drowsiness to cover the believers as security, يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً, repeating the beneficial-cover scene.
People يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمْ to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and disclose; physical covering and the hidden/manifest opposition occur together.
The faces of evildoers appear as though أُغْشِيَتْ with dark pieces of night, explicitly transferring the night-cover to human faces.
Fire تَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُم, joining the section's warning fire to the same root's action of covering faces.
ٱلْغَاشِيَةِ names the overwhelming event whose terror envelops creation, the section's widest scale for the covering root.
A غَاشِيَةٌ of God's punishment may come upon people suddenly, another explicit use of the cover as an all-enclosing event.
At the sea, فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ leaves the engulfing quantity unstated, a destructive parallel to the objectless breadth heard in 92:1.
The overturned cities are covered by مَا غَشَّىٰ, an intentionally unspecified covering that parallels the open object of 92:1 while reversing the night's neutral sign into destruction.
God wraps night over day and day over night, يُكَوِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّهَارَ عَلَى ٱلَّيْلِ, rendering their alternation as layers.
Night enters day and day enters night, and the same ayah says God knows what breasts contain; cosmic alternation and inner hiddenness are joined.
Secret and public speech are equal to God, as are one hidden by night and one moving openly by day; the physical cover models concealed and manifest human action.
Night is made a garment and sleep repose, while day is resurrection-like emergence, a concise parallel to covering followed by disclosure.
Night is made لِبَاسًا, a garment-like covering; 78:11 completes the pair by assigning visible activity to day.
Day is made مَعَاشًا for active life, supplying the opened field of action opposite the garment-night of 78:10.
The hearers are asked who could bring light if God made night continuous until Resurrection, making the cover's dependence and limit explicit.
The matching question asks who could bring night for rest if day were continuous, preserving the section's insistence that disclosure without cover is not simply good.
God's mercy appoints both night for rest and day for seeking bounty, stating the complementary purposes of the two operations.
God makes night for stillness and day مُبْصِرًا, directly pairing restorative covering with sight-giving daylight.
Night is for rest and day مُبْصِرًا; the wording makes visibility itself a feature of the daytime sign.
God makes night for rest and day مُبْصِرًا, another direct repeated formulation of the section's paired image.
God darkens the heaven's night and brings out its brightness, وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَىٰهَا, staging light as something drawn from beneath concealment.
The oath by night as it withdraws prepares the opening enacted by the breathing dawn in 81:18.
وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ pictures dawn breathing out after the retreating night of 81:17, a nonlexical parallel to day opening itself.
The oath by night when it retreats places removal of the cover immediately before the shining dawn of 74:34.
وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ makes dawn disclose and brighten, continuing the oath-pair of 92:1-2.
The oath by night وَمَا وَسَقَ presents night through what it gathers and encloses, giving the cover an inclusive object.
The oath by the bright forenoon supplies another luminous opening paired with the still night in 93:2.
The oath by night إِذَا سَجَىٰ portrays a settled cover, paired with the forenoon brightness of 93:1.
Spending is valid إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ, almost exactly joining the giver of 92:18 to the sought Face of 92:20.
The feeders act لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ and seek neither recompense nor thanks, directly matching 92:19-20's gift without a return and its sole search for the Lord's Face.
Giving relatives, the needy, and the traveler is assigned to those who seek وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ, connecting charitable action with the section's final sought Face.
Usury given to grow through people does not grow with God, while alms seeking His Face multiply; it exposes the divergent motives hidden beneath outward giving.
Those who are patient ابتغاء وجه ربهم, pray, and spend openly and secretly unite the sought Face with deeds performed across visibility and concealment.
God is the light of heavens and earth, illustrated by a lamp kindled in glass; the section's wick-derived root image becomes illumination and divine guidance here.
A breast opened to submission stands عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ, joining inward opening, light, and guidance against hardened perception.
Revelation is made a light by which God guides, نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِ, explicitly combining the section's illumination and guidance families.
One raised from death is given light to walk among people, unlike one trapped in darkness, making guidance a visible path out from covering.
وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ closely parallels إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ in assigning the direction of the path to God while acknowledging a deviating branch.
The Quran is called بَيَانٌ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى, explicitly pairing clarification with guidance exactly as the section's dictionary gloss does.
A light and a clear Book come from God after the Messenger makes hidden matters clear, joining disclosure, illumination, and revelation.
By the Book God guides seekers of His pleasure and brings them from darknesses into light, turning the cover/opening image into a path.
The ayah says eyes themselves do not go blind; hearts within breasts do, locating the decisive covering in perception as the section does.
What people earned has formed رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم, the very heart-rust invoked by the section's dictionary definition of غشاوة.
On the day people are displayed, لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ; the final opening leaves no hidden human reality beneath the common cover.
The command to act is followed by the promise that deeds will be seen and disclosed by the Knower of unseen and seen, directly realizing diverse striving made visible.
A human being has only what he strives for, giving the individual content of the سَعْيَكُمْ whose differences 92:4 announces.
That striving سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ will be seen, explicitly making hidden human effort visible before the recompense of 53:41.
The seen striving of 53:40 receives its fullest recompense here, completing the moral disclosure modeled by the opened day.
On that day the human remembers مَا سَعَىٰ, bringing the surah's human striving into conscious disclosure before 79:36 displays the Fire.
Hell is made بُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ, a warning fire brought into view after striving is recalled.
The command to set one's face toward the upright religion comes before an inescapable Day on which people يَصَّدَّعُونَ, splitting into distinct outcomes.
Stones split, يَشَّقَّقُ, and water emerges, while rivers burst from others; it gives Quranic form to the section's river cutting open the earth.
ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ شَقًّا stages the earth being split open so its hidden growth can emerge, matching the day-as-cleaving image.
The oath by وَٱلْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ makes fissuring earth itself a sign, a compact counterpart to the river/day that cracks its covering.
The ordered heavens show no fissure, and the reader is commanded to direct sight at them; 67:4 then repeats the searching gaze.
The gaze is sent back twice and returns exhausted, a close Quranic counterpart to the dictionary image of casting a sharpened look like a hunting falcon.
وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ pictures heaven stripped of its covering, the cosmic form of the veil being removed.
Faces are radiant on that Day, supplying the uncovered, luminous face opposite faces overlaid by night-darkness.
Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, bringing face, cleared sight, and the divine object sought in 92:20 into one scene.
Other faces bear dust on that Day, beginning a facial covering completed by darkness in 80:41.
تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ says darkness overspreads those dust-covered faces, a close nonlexical parallel to 10:27's pieces of night.
The neglected person's covering is removed and sight becomes حَدِيدٌ, simultaneously reversing the veil and joining sharpened vision to the dictionary's polished blade.
Neither darkness nor humiliation يَرْهَقُ the faces of the doers of beauty, the precise positive boundary reversed in 10:27.
Layered sea, wave, cloud, and darkness leave a person unable to see even his hand; without God's light there is no light, the full reversal of self-revealing day.
After heart-rust in 83:14, the rejecters are veiled from their Lord, setting a limit opposite the disclosure and Lord-facing sight of 7:143 and 75:23.
God's communication may occur from behind a veil, establishing the protective boundary around divine disclosure that the mountain scene demonstrates.
Vision does not encompass God though He encompasses vision, qualifying the image of cleared sight at the point of divine self-disclosure.
Thamud were guided but preferred blindness over guidance, making refusal to see after clarification an explicit chosen reversal.
The blind and the seeing are declared unequal, giving a human boundary to the section's distinction between covered and opened sight.
Darknesses and light are declared unequal, the cosmic counterpart to the unequal perceivers of 35:19.
The ayah asks whether the blind equals the seeing or darknesses equal light, using visibility to expose false equivalence.
Other faces on that Day are gloomy, the facial reversal of the radiant faces in 75:22.
Those gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity, supplying the inward recognition beneath their darkened appearance.
The sky is split open with clouds on the Last Day; the clouds reverse the dictionary's cloudless clear sky even as the covering itself is opened.
The present sky is contemplated as having no fissures, a boundary opposite the cracked earth and stripped or split heaven elsewhere in the image.
The opening oath identifies the sun that the pronouns in 91:3-4 respectively disclose and cover.
God inserts night into day and day into night, presenting their boundary as a continuously moving overlap rather than a fixed division.
Night entering day and day entering night grounds divine support in the same reciprocal passage between cover and opening.
The mutual entering of night and day is set beside the ordered courses of sun and moon, locating the image in measured creation.
Night and day enter one another while sun and moon run to appointed terms, emphasizing the measured duration of each layer.
God alternates night and day, and the ayah calls this a lesson for those with sight, directly making visual perception the intended response.
God takes people by night, knows what they earn by day, and raises them in it until their return and disclosure; nightly concealment frames visible striving.
Sleep by night and day and seeking God's bounty are paired signs, adding human rest and action to the cosmic alternation.
The oath by dawn supplies the opening edge of the night that passes in 89:4.
The oath by night as it journeys away makes the cover temporary and directs attention toward dawn in 89:1.
Seeking refuge in the Lord of daybreak invokes the One who splits open the morning against the settling darkness named in 113:3.
The evil of darkness إِذَا وَقَبَ presents night as an entering, surrounding condition, while 113:1 names the Lord of its breach.
The Night of Decree is peace until the emergence of dawn, a concrete instance of a beneficent night-cover bounded by daybreak.
Eyes are described as being فِى غِطَآءٍ from God's remembrance, a semantic counterpart to the غشاوة that blocks perception.
Rejecters claim coverings over their hearts and a veil between themselves and the messenger, extending the eye membrane into resistant inward hearing.
Recitation places a concealed veil between the Prophet and those who deny the Hereafter, presenting revelation itself as a boundary for resistant hearers.
Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears explain the perceptual veil of 17:45 and the refusal produced when God alone is named.
Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears prevent understanding even while the rejecters outwardly listen, another inner form of remaining under the cover.
Noah's people cover themselves with garments while refusing his call, a deliberate act of staying covered when clarification arrives.
A visible smoke يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ and is recognized as painful punishment, making a physical atmospheric cover into warning.
Punishment covers the rejecters from above and beneath their feet, a spatial analogue to the all-enclosing غاشية.
Canopies of fire stand above and below the damned, giving the warning fire the architecture of a surrounding cover.
Immediately beneath the named غاشية, some faces are humbled, showing the overwhelming cover registered on faces.
Other faces on that same Day are joyful, preserving the divergent outcomes revealed beneath the one overwhelming event.
A Day when faces whiten and blacken makes opposed inward histories visibly legible on the face.
Brightened faces enter mercy permanently, completing the positive branch opposite 3:106's darkened faces.
Following God's guidance prevents straying and misery; the next ayat show turning away ending in blind resurrection.
Turning from remembrance leads to a constricted life and being raised blind, connecting rejected guidance to lost sight.
The resurrected blind person protests that he once possessed sight, exposing the difference between worldly eyesight and perception after the cover is removed.
The answer says God's signs came and were forgotten, explaining the blindness of 20:124-125 as refused disclosure.
The Prophet cannot guide the blind out of error; only responsive believers hear, binding guidance to receptive sight and hearing.
This repeated formulation says the Prophet cannot guide the blind from error, confirming the link between guidance and unsealed perception.
The address asks whether the Prophet can make the deaf hear or guide the blind, marking the limit of human warning when faculties are covered.
The Quran is guidance and healing to believers, but heaviness and blindness to rejecters as though they are called from far away.
On the day secrets are tested, what lay beneath the human exterior is brought into judgment.
People issue forth in separate groups so their deeds may be shown to them, directly joining visible disclosure with differentiated courses.
Even an atom's weight of good is seen, specifying how fully the disclosed striving of 99:6 becomes visible.
Even an atom's weight of evil is seen, completing the other branch of the disclosed distinction.
Graves are scattered open, beginning an outer unveiling that reaches what breasts conceal in 100:10.
What is within breasts is extracted and exposed, an inward analogue to daylight bringing what lay under a cover into prominence.
The record is laid open and people find every deed present, a judgment scene in which concealed striving becomes readable.
Each person acts according to his own disposition while the Lord knows who is best guided, a direct statement of differentiated human courses.
God shows the human being the way, after which he is either grateful or ungrateful; one disclosed path yields two stances.
The soul is shown both its depravity and its piety, supplying the paired possibilities that become divergent striving in the next surah.
Success belongs to one who purifies the soul, the first visible outcome of the opposition introduced in 91:8.
Failure belongs to one who buries the soul, turning concealment into the contrary outcome to purification.
The Quran contains guidance and clear proofs of guidance and criterion, supporting the section's reading of huda as clarification.
The Book is sent to clarify what people differed about and as guidance, linking disclosure of divergence with huda.
The Book is described as clarification of all things and guidance, another explicit Quranic pairing of البيان and الهدى.
The Book brings people from darknesses into light by their Lord's permission, translating night-to-day opening into revelation.
God brings believers from darknesses into light, while false patrons take people from light into darknesses, preserving both directions of the image.
Clear signs are sent to bring people from darknesses into light, combining clarification with passage out from covering.
A messenger recites clarifying signs to bring believing doers from darknesses into light, adding visible action to the passage.
Those who call on their Lord morning and evening seek His Face, joining the sought Face with the daily boundary times.
The Prophet is told to remain with those who call morning and evening seeking their Lord's Face, repeating the temporal and devotional meeting.
Everything perishes except God's Face, giving permanence to the Face sought at the end of a surah opened by passing night and day.
The majestic Face of the Lord remains while what is on earth passes, the lasting term beyond the alternating cover and opening.
The challengers demand that rivers be made to gush through the earth, a forceful Quranic scene of water opening land.
A river is caused to gush between two gardens, concretizing the river's opening course through cultivated ground.
The earth is burst into springs and its waters meet the descending flood, a large-scale water-through-earth counterpart to the river image.
The sky is opened into gates on the Last Day, expanding the section's opened surface from day and earth to heaven.
The sky splitting open is an eschatological version of the covering layer being breached.
The sky is split and heeds its Lord, another judgment-day opening of what now covers the visible world.
Even if a gate in heaven were opened and the rejecters ascended through it, 15:15 says they would deny their own sight.
The rejecters answer an opened heaven by claiming their eyes are intoxicated or bewitched, showing disclosure can occur without willing perception.
At judgment the earth shines with the light of its Lord and the record is placed, joining divine light with the final exposure of deeds.
Hell is brought forth visibly to the deviators, another warning fire disclosed rather than hidden.
The question of who guards people by night and day plausibly adds protection to both periods, though it does not itself portray night as the protecting cover.
Revelation occurring in the Night of Decree plausibly reinforces that night-cover is not intrinsically adverse; the connection depends on the section's stated moral neutrality of night.
